key_insight: Extending multi-pass weld stops away from the gusset joint and TIG dressing their notches substantially improved fatigue strength compared with conventional welded-around gussets.
engineering_relevance: The technique offers a route to more fatigue-resistant gusset end details, with FAT90 (m = 5) provisionally suggested for design at R = 0.5.
method: Screened welding and post-weld treatments using S420 steel coupon fatigue tests.
Tested the selected extended-weld and TIG-dressed configuration under constant-amplitude loading at R = 0.1.
Evaluated similar joints under variable-amplitude block loading in the high-cycle regime.
evidence_signal: Constant-amplitude tests yielded a characteristic fatigue strength of 127 MPa at 97.7% survival probability with slope m = 5; variable-amplitude tests provided additional validation.
watch_item: The FAT90 design recommendation relies on mean-stress transformation and preliminary finite-element analysis, so applicability to other geometries and loading conditions needs verification.
paper_title: Fatigue strength improvement of gusset end detail with welding techniques
